instructions: Finely chop the onions. Mince the garlic and grate 1 tbsp of the ginger. Cut the beef into 1 1/2-inch cubes, pat them dry, and toss them with 1 tsp of the salt and the pepper.

Heat 1 tbsp of the ghee in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add half the beef in a single layer and leave it alone until the underside is deep brown, about 4 minutes. Turn the pieces and brown them for 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate and brown the second half the same way.

Turn the heat to medium. Add the onions, 1/4 cup water and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt to the same pot. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onions are soft and just starting to turn golden. Add a splash of water if they start to stick.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp ghee, the garlic and the ginger. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the turmeric and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant. Keep it moving so it doesn't clump.

Return the beef and its juices to the pot, add 2 cups of water, and bring to a simmer. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 1 hour, stirring now and then, until the beef is tender when you press it with a spoon.
Meanwhile, about 25 minutes before the beef is done, rinse the rice and cook it according to the package.
Take the lid off for the last 10 minutes if the sauce is thin. It should be thick enough to coat the beef.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the cardamom. Slice the jalapeño into rings and put them in a small bowl for anyone who wants heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice or with injera, and the jalapeño on the table.
method_notes: No version I could read showed a rating, so this is a fallback lead: Tara's Multicultural Table mild lamb stew (4 stars from 1 vote) is the closest real alicha, with onions, ginger, garlic, turmeric, coriander and cardamom and no berbere. The Wikibooks alicha wot browns the beef before the spices. I used beef as the dish asks, browned it first, left out the coriander and used a smaller pinch of cardamom (a reader of the lead found the cardamom too strong), and kept the sauce thick since the lead's water amounts disagree.
